thread:
leo: Planning a coordinated deploy tonight 02:00 UTC. Components: API v2.3, runtime kernel toggle, console prefetch, router header-split. Need pin step and a brief prewarm before broad traffic.
anya: Acknowledged. I'll pin the console to 2.3-rc and add a conservative cache fallback.
carmen: Router will need a short-lived routing rule for /internal-prefetch to target the canary pool. Can we avoid global config flips?
leo: Yes, temporary route only for the prefetch window. Deploy plan: canary 5% at 02:10 for 10m, observe, then 25% at 02:30. Rollback if 5xx > 0.5% or p95 > 600ms for 5 minutes.
devbot: Scheduled: canary @ 02:10. Health checks enabled: 5xx rate, latency p95, error-rate-by-route.
sylvie: Runtime team: kernel batch switch + KV eviction tuning. Expect warmup latency for small sequences. We'll add a batch-ramp toggle to smooth behavior.
opsbot: Preflight checks: certs valid, DB migration N/A, feature-flag config set to runtime:new_kernels=false by default.
leo: Console prefetch approach: run prefetch against canary after initial canary warmup. One-off endpoint: POST /internal/prefetch?scope=canary with OP token. Add X-Test-Canary header for router identification.
anya: Will queue the job. But we need the router to pin that path to canary otherwise prefetch hits main pool. Router owners?
carmen: Can add a short-lived rule. ETA ~6m. Will set TTL 10m on pin. Also add a header check to avoid accidental pinning from prod traffic.
sylvie: We'll emit a metric runtime.kv.prefetch_miss and a header X-KV-Fallback=true when fallback path used. Console will honor that header for telemetry.
devbot: Canary started. 0/50 checks failing. Tracking p50/p95 and kv.prefetch_miss.
devbot: Canary update (02:15): p95 climbed to 680ms, 2/50 checks failing, no 5xx. Marking canary HOLD.
leo: Hold. If this is warmup noise we can enable console fallback and see if user impact is mitigated. No rollback yet.
carmen: Router logs show extra latency concentrated on /generate endpoints. No spike in 5xx. Likely kernel JIT/runtime warmup.
anya: Flipping console fallback flag now so UI uses cached values when prefetch misses. That should mask user-facing latency.
sylvie: After enabling conservative batch-ramp (slower batch size growth) p95 dropped to 490ms on canary. kv.prefetch_miss fell from ~12% to ~3% after fallback and retry.
devbot: Canary health recovered. Recommendation: resume to 25% at 02:30.
leo: Decision: resume rollout with monitoring extended to 3h post-rollout. Add note to release changelog: "Known warmup latency with new runtime kernel; mitigations: console prefetch + fallback and batch-ramp applied."
anya: I'll publish a short ops how-to for customers running private deploys (prefetch endpoint + X-KV-Fallback usage).
carmen: Router temporary rule removed after prefetch window. Confirmed no residual pins.
devbot: Rollout to 25% started. Full rollout scheduled at 03:00 if no regressions.
leo: If any service breaches thresholds, open #incidents and tag eng-sre immediately. Postmortem: include timeline of kernel toggle, prefetch metrics, and fallback events.
anya: Added short bullet to release notes and pinned the console docs update.
sylvie: We'll keep kv.prefetch_miss and X-KV-Fallback traces for 72h. If downstream customers report latency, we may rollback kernel flag.
leo: Thanks team. Stand down unless alerts fire.
